transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, it's nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

If you looked at my kitchen table right now, it's completely covered. There are my husband’s appointment papers, flyers from church, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists I've started. I sit down there to try and sort it out, and I just don't know which thing to do first. I end up just sitting there looking at it all until the whole day is gone.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

Yes, quite a bit, actually. It feels like things just slip my mind completely once they're out of sight. I’ve missed returning phone calls, and I've left bills sitting right under a stack of mail and just forgotten they were there. 

I've also forgotten errands I specifically promised my daughter I’d do for her. And... well, more than once, I've realized way too late that I never actually called to confirm one of my husband’s appointments. I just forget to do these things.
Have you had problems with attention and staying organized since you were younger?

Yes, actually. It's been a problem for as long as I can remember. Even when I was a little girl... I remember my teachers writing notes to my parents saying I was bright, but careless. I was always forgetting my books or leaving my homework behind. They constantly had to give me reminders to just finish my seatwork before I could go outside to play. So, it's definitely not a new issue for me.
Do these problems with attention and organization cause difficulties for you in more than one part of your life now, not just at home?

Yes, they do. It's definitely not just at home. I actually had to give up leading a big event down at the senior center recently because I just couldn't manage it all. 

And... well, it's affecting things with my family, too. My daughter has started double-checking the bills and my husband's appointments. She just doesn't trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore.
Have these attention and organization problems gotten noticeably worse in recent years?

Yes, they really have. The trouble has been this bad for... well, about a year and three months now. That's when my husband's health changed and he started needing me to help him regularly with all his appointments and daily arrangements. Before that, I could mostly get by, but since I took on managing his schedule on top of everything else, it's just become too much to keep track of.
Have you been diagnosed with any neurological or other medical illness that affected your thinking or memory?

No, I haven't. I mean, I go to my regular check-ups, but they've never diagnosed me with anything like that. No strokes or... well, dementia or anything that would mess with my memory. Physically, I'm actually doing fine. It's really just this trouble with my focus and trying to keep everything organized.
Compared with how you were a few years ago, do you feel your thinking and memory have clearly gotten worse?

No, I don't think so. I mean... my memory itself is actually fine. I remember things just as well as I did a few years ago. It's really just what I was saying before—it's the focus. My brain just gets overloaded trying to organize all the details now. But my actual thinking and memory... no, I wouldn't say they've gotten worse.
